remediation.title: Unreadable Linux swap inventory suppresses the secret-memory warning
remediation.correction: SwapInventory::Unavailable preserves a failed read; the settings warning names unknown encryption. A readable empty inventory remains silent. Existing visible plaintext/unknown-device escaping and encrypted/zram classifications remain in the scoped tests.
remediation.verification: Missing and directory-valued synthetic inventories and an injected PermissionDenied result are distinguished from a readable empty inventory. Warning strings and visible-area escaping/classification are checked. No actual swap paging, storage read or secret extraction.
remediation.formalClosure: Pending a signed fix/verification commit; fixed is a working-tree disposition, not formal verified closure. Original AUD-020 remains open at its reviewed snapshot.

remediation.title: Generated password can reach the main Windows console when VT activation fails
remediation.correction: Shared terminal eligibility now requires VT capability. After acquiring PrivateScreen, the common generated-password sink refuses unless shows_privately() confirms an actual or enclosing private screen, before any password text is written.
remediation.verification: Before the patch, the isolated no-terminal regression detected generated-password output; afterward it confirms refusal and no output. Scoped PTY acceptance covers the shared words/check-word/chars display and enclosing flow according to the recorded harness output. Windows VT API failure, console retention and real Windows runtime remain unexecuted.
remediation.formalClosure: Pending a signed fix/verification commit; fixed is a working-tree disposition, not formal verified closure. Original AUD-020 remains open at its reviewed snapshot.

limitations: Both fixes and scoped regressions pass in the dirty working tree; no signed fix or verification commit was requested or created. Formal status remains fixed, not verified.
Original three failing assertions remain in before-swap/before-display logs. They were regression runs after tests were added, not new findings or passing baseline checks.
No actual Windows VT activation failure, Windows/macOS runtime, console retention, forced paging, swap storage read or secret extraction was exercised.
Injected PermissionDenied and missing/directory synthetic procfs inventories test error handling, not host encryption itself.
No new full security scan, full-cost Argon2/vector replay, real browser suite, canonical Docker/WASM rebuild, release verification or publication. Algorithm, formats and public APIs did not change.
Terminal control support cannot guarantee privacy on a hostile terminal/host; the new guard proves the program refuses an inactive private-screen state in the tested path.
Local raw evidence is unchanged and ignored. Published home paths are anonymized; local-only artifacts are not public downloadable assets.
assessment: Both original Low findings are fixed with passing scoped dirty-source verification. No new finding IDs or release-acceptance claim; signed-commit formal closure remains pending.
